images.caption: Figure 1:Comparison of VLA, WAM, andnanoAstra. Unlike VLA and WAM, which rely on dense control-step prediction,nanoAstraorganizes robot behavior into reusable semantic steps with explicit progress guidance and executable actions.

Figure 2:Overview of thenanoAstradata pipeline. Heterogeneous demonstrations are filtered, geometrically standardized, segmented into subtasks, and converted into semantic steps before mixing with general vision-language data. The example illustrates how observations at behavioral decision points are paired with progress descriptions and executable action primitives.

Figure 3:Camera re-calibration.We project the robot model at the recorded joint states into the camera image, giving arm masks and end-effector (EEF) points.Left:with the original extrinsics they are offset from the arms; red segments connect each projected EEF point to the EEF’s actual image location (red dot).Right:after re-calibration they align more closely with the arms, which also reduces the EEF reprojection error.
Figure 8:Failure cases ofnanoAstraon RoboTwin 2.0. Each frame shows the decision turn and the predicted progress.
